name: FreeCell
intro: Learn FreeCell from scratch: the layout, building down in alternating colours, free cells, foundations and moving runs, then freeing aces and winning empty columns.

units.name: How FreeCell works
units.blurb: The layout, building down, free cells, foundations and moving runs.

lessons.title: The FreeCell layout
lessons.summary: FreeCell deals all 52 cards face up into eight columns, with four free cells and four foundations above. Learn the layout and the goal.
lessons.wrap: Every card is visible, so every deal is a puzzle. Next: building in the columns.

steps.text:
FreeCell deals all 52 cards face up into eight columns. Above them are four free cells (on the left) and four foundations (on the right).

The goal is to move every card to the foundations, building each suit up from ace to king. The lessons show just part of a deal.
Quick check.
steps.prompt: How much of the deal can you see at the start?
options: Only the top card of each column
steps.explain: Every card. That’s why FreeCell is all skill: almost every deal can be won.

lessons.title: Building down in alternating colours
lessons.summary: In FreeCell’s columns you build down in alternating colours: a red 6 on a black 7. Learn the rule and practise a move.
lessons.wrap: One lower, opposite colour. Next: the free cells.

steps.text: You can move the top card of a column onto another column if it’s one rank lower and the opposite colour: a red 6 on a black 7, then a black 5 on the red 6.
Tap a card, then the column to move it to.
steps.prompt: Build one card onto another column.
steps.wrong: The card must be one lower and the opposite colour.

lessons.title: Free cells and foundations
lessons.summary: A free cell holds any one card for later, and aces start the foundations. Learn to use a free cell to dig out an ace.
lessons.wrap: Cells are parking spaces; foundations are where cards finish. Next: moving runs.

steps.text:
Each free cell holds one card. Any top card can go there, and come back to a column later.

The ace of hearts is buried under the 4 of spades, and the 4 can’t be built anywhere.
Park the 4 in a free cell.
steps.prompt: Move the 4 of spades to a free cell.
steps.wrong: Tap the 4 of spades, then an empty free cell.

steps.text: Aces start the foundations.
steps.prompt: Move the ace to a foundation.
steps.wrong: Tap the ace, then a foundation.

steps.text: Foundations build up by suit: ace, 2, 3…
steps.prompt: Send a card to its foundation.
steps.wrong: Which card is next for the hearts or spades foundation?

lessons.title: Moving runs and empty columns
lessons.summary: You move one card at a time, but free cells and empty columns let you move a whole ordered run. Learn how many cards you can move.
lessons.wrap: You know every rule. Test yourself in the rules check.

steps.text:
Officially you move one card at a time. But with free spaces you can move an ordered run card by card, so the game does it in one go.

With f empty free cells and e empty columns, you can move up to (f + 1) × 2e cards. Each empty column doubles it. An empty column can also take any card or run.
You have 2 empty free cells and 1 empty column.
steps.prompt: How many cards can you move onto another column at once?

units.name: Rules check
units.blurb: Five questions on the rules. Pass to unlock the strategy.

lessons.title: FreeCell rules check
lessons.summary: Test your FreeCell rules: building down in alternating colours, free cells, foundations, empty columns and moving runs.
lessons.wrap: Rules check passed. Now for the planning.

steps.text: Question 1.
steps.prompt: Can a black 5 go on a black 6?

steps.text: Question 2.
steps.prompt: Move the 7 of clubs onto a red 8.

steps.text: Question 3.
steps.prompt: How many cards fit in one free cell?

steps.text: Question 4.
steps.prompt: Move a card to a foundation.

steps.text: Question 5.
steps.prompt: With 3 empty free cells and no empty columns, how many cards can you move at once?

units.name: Planning
units.blurb: Free the aces, keep cells empty and win an empty column.

lessons.title: Free the aces first
lessons.summary: Aces and 2s buried deep block everything. Learn to look for them before you move, and to dig them out with column moves.
lessons.wrap: Find the aces before your first move, and dig them out.

steps.text:
Before your first move, find the aces and 2s and count the cards on top of each. The fewer, the sooner you can free them.

Here the ace of diamonds is under just one card, and that card can be built onto another column.
Don’t use a free cell if a column will do.
steps.prompt: Uncover the ace without using a free cell.
steps.wrong: Move the 5 of spades onto a red 6.
steps.done: The ace is uncovered, and all four cells are still empty.

steps.text: Now the ace can go up.
steps.wrong: Tap the ace, then a foundation.

lessons.title: Keep free cells empty
lessons.summary: Every card in a free cell cuts how many cards you can move. Learn to treat cells as short-term parking, not storage.
lessons.wrap: Use a cell only when it wins you something, and empty it soon.

steps.text: Every card in a free cell cuts how many cards you can move at once: with 4 empty cells you can move 5 cards, but with 2 empty cells only 3.
steps.prompt: When should you put a card in a free cell?
options: Whenever it has nowhere else to go
Only when it frees something useful, like an ace or a whole column
steps.explain: Only when it gains you something. A cell full of stuck cards is how deals are lost.

lessons.title: Win an empty column
lessons.summary: An empty column doubles how many cards you can move. Learn to spot the shortest column and clear it without filling your free cells.
lessons.wrap: Clear the shortest column early, and keep it empty for big moves.

steps.text:
An empty column is worth more than any free cell: it doubles how many cards you can move, and it can hold a whole run.

Look for the shortest column, especially one whose cards can be built elsewhere.
The column with just the 4 of spades is the shortest.
steps.prompt: Empty a column without using a free cell.
steps.wrong: Build the 4 of spades onto a red 5.
steps.done: An empty column, and every free cell still free.
